Recommended weight 153cm: 45-68kg (100-150 lbs) [3] 71. Recommended weight 157cm: 63-81kg (140-180 lbs) [3] 72. Recommended weight 160cm: 68-90kg (150-200 lbs) [3] 73. Recommended weight 156cm Wide: 63-90kg (140-200 lbs) [3] 74. Recommended weight 159cm Wide: 68-100kg (150-200 lbs) [3] 75. Recommended weight 162cm Wide: 77-108+kg (170-240+ lbs) [3] 76. Nose/tail design: Wider, elongated tips with steeper/higher kicks — swallowtail-esque shape mirrored for twin [4][6] 77. Camber type: Triple Camber Hybrid [3] 78. Camber description: Overall central rocker shape with camber zone in between, creating two high-pressure rocker sections on each side of middle camber [3] 79. Triple Camber detail: Three camber sections — one between the feet (center), two under the feet — flanked by small rockers, with early rise at tip and tail [23][24] 80. Patented technology: Never Summer holds the first-ever patent on hybrid camber technology (September 2010) [25] 81. Edge hold technology: R.I.P. Edge Hold Technology — integrates waves into the base creating high-pressure points for smooth drag-free rides [3] 82. R.I.P. Edge Hold mechanism: Edge hold starts at center of board and is derived from the base plane instead of protruding out from the edges [4] 83. Sidecut type: Power Grip Sidecut (Vario) — multiple radii with flat section in middle, shallow radii on sides, deeper radii near tips [3] 84. Extended Transition Area: Small flat section in the snowboard profile that improves both turn initiation and powder flotation [3][19] 85. Mounting pattern: 2x4 Inserts [3] 86. Flex rating: 6/10 (1=soft, 10=stiff) [3] 87. Flex feel on snow (independent review): Mid-Soft 4.5/10 — feels softer than the rated 6 [26] (DISAGREEMENT: The merchant/manufacturer lists flex as 6/10 but an independent reviewer found it felt like 4.5/10 on snow. This discrepancy may reflect the difference between manufacturer's static flex rating and real-world feel.) 88. Dampness rating: 5/10 (1=lively, 10=damp) [18] 89. Core material: NS SuperLight Wood Core — Poplar, Paulownia, and Birch [3] 90. Core construction: CNC sanded to a fraction of a millimeter in custom woodworking facility [19] 91. Core wood species detail: High percentage of lightweight Paulownia combined with Poplar and Birch running down the middle; Poplar along the sidecut edge [5] 92. Fiberglass type 1: Bi-Lite Fiberglass — combines STS strength characteristics with ultralight glass fiber matrix [19] 93. Fiberglass type 2: STS Pre-Tensioned Fiberglass — elastomer stringers between glass fibers for strength and edge hold [3] 94. Carbon technology: Full Recluse Carbon Web Layup — carbon fiber at 20-degree angles for torsional stability, edge hold pressure, and longitudinal rebound [3][4] 95. Carbon flex retention: Recluse Carbon Web Technology holds the integrity of the board's flex pattern over a longer period of time [4] 96. Dampening system: Triple Layer RDS 2 Damping with Underfoot Stabiliser [3] 97. RDS 2 description: Three narrow layers providing an ideal combination of vibration absorption and stability, bridging freestyle and freeride damping [19] 98. Underfoot stabiliser: Elastomeric Underfoot Stabilisers beneath mounting area for shock/vibration absorption, high-speed stability, reduced foot fatigue [3] 99. Sidewall material: UHMW Sidewalls (Ultra High Molecular Weight Polyethylene) [3] 100. Sidewall advantage: More resistant to cracking in cold temperatures than conventional ABS; improved damping [3][19] 101. Sidewall innovation: Never Summer was first snowboard company to use and perfect Sintered P-Tex sidewalls [19] 102. Topsheet: Co-Extruded Polymer Topsheet — tough lightweight thermoplastic with fiber backing, scratch/chip resistant, vivid colors, built-in stomp pad grip [3] 103. Edges: Fullwrap Metal Edge with Aluminium Nose and Tail protectors [3] 104. Base material: Durasurf XT Sintered 5501 Base — infused with graphite, high performance sintered [3] 105. Base description: Proprietary Crown Plastics exclusive super fast durable sintered base, fastest Never Summer has ever used [19] 106. Additional features: Extended Transition Area, P-Tex Nose/Tail Protection [3] 107. Overall ride character: Effortless, responsive to the slightest energy; doesn't like when overpowered [26] 108. Turning ease: Super easy to initiate turns; almost too easy at times — "the board was trying to turn before you were ready" [26] 109. Edge hold on ice (MtnWeekly review): "Edge hold felt close to a 10 out of 10" [27] 110. Edge hold on ice (customer review): "V Twin offered more edge control than all the trad-camber boards I just rode" [28] 111. Carving performance: Mixed — nice and fun at slow speed, gets washy when leaning over aggressively at speed [26] 112. Carving spring out of turn (TheGoodRide): "It will hold but doesn't have that spring out of the turn" [29] 113. Speed stability: Speed wobbles emerge at moderate-to-high speeds; not terrible but noticeable [26] 114. High speed chatter: May have some tip/tail chatter at very high speed (~60mph), but chatter quiets down as it gets to feet [5][29] 115. Dampening feel (TheGoodRide): "Never Summer just has amazing dampness… more damp overall compared to most" peers at same flex rating [29] 116. Pop access: Ultra easy to access pop; "could just think about popping it and it would respond" [26] 117. Pop level: Pretty good but not epic — decent total pop for how easy it is to access [26] 118. Pop consistency (MtnWeekly CON): Inconsistent/unpredictable pop on side hits and firm natural takeoffs, attributed to triple camber profile [27] 119. Triple camber hooky feel (TheGoodRide): "The three camber profiles can fight each other a little bit. It's something you need to get used to" [29] 120. Forgiveness: Despite hooky feel, it hooks but doesn't catch a lot; forgiving of skewed landings [29][26] 121. Switch riding: Really good for switch with easy transitions; felt very similar both ways [26] 122. Buttering/pressing: Nice and easy to press tip and tail; feels very similar to press both ends; easy to lock in [26] 123. Jibbing: Really good — easy pop onto/off features; looser feeling can cause slide-out more than expected [26] 124. Powder performance: Not specifically a powder board; surfier feel and rocker help in shallow powder; would struggle in deep powder [26] 125. Powder float (manufacturer claim): Elongated tips add surface area to float in deep powder [4] 126. Trees/tight terrain: Super agile for weaving tight lines; excellent in trees [26][29] 127. Groomer performance: Remarkable edge hold on groomed runs; smooth underfoot feel [27] 128. Landing stability: Felt wobbly with landings from bigger jumps [26] 129. Base glide (TheGoodRide): "Not the fastest of fast, but when well waxed, they're definitely upper tier and better than most boards at this price point" [29] 130. Durability (TheGoodRide): "Very durable construction and one of the best topsheets in the industry" [29] 131. Weight feel: On the light side of normal; slightly lighter than average [26][29] 132. Board weight (measured by SnowboardingProfiles, 157cm): 3120g (6 lbs 14 oz) [26] 133. Weight per cm (157cm): 19.87 g/cm versus 18.64 g/cm average for 300+ boards tested [26] 134. Graphic/aesthetics: Viking longship design between bindings; Valhalla insignia; unique bat-wing tip/tail shape draws frequent compliments [5][28] 135. Topsheet durability: Very durable; co-extruded polymer tastefully designed [5] 136. SnowboardingProfiles overall score: 86.7/100 [26] 137. SnowboardingProfiles ranking: 12th out of 33 all-mountain-freestyle boards tested [26] 138. SnowboardingProfiles jumps score: 4/5 (16/20 weighted) [26] 139. SnowboardingProfiles carving score: 3/5 (6/10 weighted) [26] 140. SnowboardingProfiles turns score: 4.5/5 (9/10 weighted) [26] 141. SnowboardingProfiles switch score: 4.5/5 (9/10 weighted) [26] 142. SnowboardingProfiles speed score: 3/5 (6/10 weighted) [26] 143. SnowboardingProfiles spins score: 4.5/5 (9/10 weighted) [26] 144. SnowboardingProfiles butters score: 4.5/5 (9/10 weighted) [26] 145. SnowboardingProfiles jibbing score: 4/5 (4/5 weighted) [26] 146. SnowboardingProfiles crud score: 3/5 (3/5 weighted) [26] 147. SnowboardingProfiles trees score: 4.5/5 (4.5/5 weighted) [26] 148. SnowboardingProfiles powder score: 2.5/5 (2.5/5 weighted) [26] 149. TheGoodRide summary: "Easy turning, playful, forgiving mtn freestyle ride with exceptional grip" [29] 150. MtnWeekly summary: "Top shelf, unique looking, very fun and capable freestyle/freeride deck" [27] 151. MtnWeekly ideal rider: "Made for the rider who is hitting jumps 60-70% of their time on snow" [27] 152. MtnWeekly one-board-quiver assessment: "A great daily driver and for the right person it could be a one board quiver" [27] 153. OldGuysRipToo recommendation: "Intermediate to expert rider looking for a unique shape and top performing mid flex snowboard" [5] 154. OldGuysRipToo flex verdict: "I found the flex to be superb for freestyle and carving" [5] 155. Customer review (NS site): "The ultimate go anywhere, do anything resort board… this board crushes all of it" [28] 156. Customer review - forgiving: "Very forgiving which helps a lot cause I'm not an expert level rider" [28] 157. Customer review - edge hold: "V Twin offered more edge control than all the trad-camber boards" [28] 158. Customer review - attention grabbing: "This board draws attention, people are always commenting on it" [28] 159. Customer service reputation: Praised consistently — "customer service has been amazing" with responsive chat support [28] 160. Warranty issue rate (dealer report): A Whistler dealer reported only 2 warranty issues in 7-9 years selling Never Summers [30] 161. Customer loyalty: Multiple reviews mention becoming "forever" NS owners after trying triple camber [28] 162. Rider level: Intermediate-Advanced [3] 163. Target rider (Boardsport SOURCE): "OG customer base for the true hard charging riders that are putting in the days riding" [7] 164. Terrain suitability: All Mountain, Freestyle, Freeride [3] 165. Best suited for: Getting creative and playful all over the mountain — park laps, side-hits, trees, natural features [26] 166. Not best for: Bombing and carving trenches at high speed; deep powder days (use Proto FR instead) [26][28] 167. Not for beginners: Looser feeling takes skill to control; responds to very light touch [26] 168. Recommended boot sizes (TheGoodRide): 153: US 8-9, 157: US 9-10, 160: US 9.5-10.5, 156X: US 10-11, 159X: US 10.5-11.5, 162X: US 11-12 [29] 169. Sizing note (TheGoodRide): NS weight recommendations are "a little too conservative" [29] 170. Competitor: CAPiTA DOA (Defenders of Awesome): True twin, Flex 6/10, camber-dominant, more park-focused than V-Twin; $549.95; Good Wood Award winner [31] 171. Competitor: Jones Mountain Twin: Directional twin with camber profile and serrated edges; $579.95; better in powder with 3D nose and setback; more versatile in deep snow [31] 172. Competitor: CAPiTA Mercury: Felt quicker, nimbler, more lively than NS by a forum user; base is much faster; more confidence-inspiring per comparison [32] 173. Competitor: Never Summer Proto Type 3: Same brand, Triple Camber Recurve (different profile variant), $699.99; better for east coast ice grip; has setback "Blower Stance" inserts for powder days the V-Twin lacks [33] 174. Competitor: Never Summer Easy Rider: Same brand, softer flex, more accessible/forgiving triple camber for all levels; $689.99 [2] 175. Competitor: Never Summer Valhalla: Directional version, the V-Twin's parent board; $709.99; better for powder/freeride with taper and setback [17] 176. Forum criticism of NS boards generally: "Pretty dead under foot since they are so damp" — some forum users prefer the liveliness of Capita boards [32] 177. NS vs competitors - dampness advantage: "If you were to compare the same flex rating to other peers in the industry, this would be a little more damp overall compared to most" [29] 178. NS vs competitors - durability advantage: Never Summer known for "bullet proof" construction; boards "will last a long time" [29][32] 179. NS vs competitors - price positioning: At $699.99, the V-Twin is "relatively high, potentially making it inaccessible to some riders" [27] 180. Brand reputation: One of the most trusted snowboard brands since 1991; known for quality, durability, and customer service [8] 181. Manufacturing philosophy: Focused on product and rider first; quality, durability, craftsmanship; domestic manufacturing [7] 182. US manufacturing advantage: Can prototype and have it on snow within 5-6 days; quick marketplace reactions [13] 183. Industry position: Only other major US snowboard maker is Mervin Industries (Gnu, Lib Tech, Roxy) backed by private equity [13] 184. Innovation legacy: First patent on hybrid camber technology; innovators of P-Tex sidewalls [25] 185. UK distributor: Maxtrack [34] 186. Triple Camber sales trend: "All our models featuring our Triple Camber profiles with the RIP edge tech are definitely seeing growth and early sales have been strong" [7] 187. Tariff impact: As a US-manufactured board using globally sourced raw materials, faces tariff and shipping cost pressures; "battling price increases" is biggest challenge [7] 188. Factory tours: Free tours available at Denver factory (Mon-Fri) [11]
